## Construct a MeshBlock and its modules (`MeshBlockOptions`) {#sec-ch01-construction}

### Summary

A `MeshBlock` is the unit that owns a grid patch and every module that acts on it. Constructing one takes an options
tree, from a YAML[^rg-f2bec48375b7] card or from Python. The constructor resolves the global grid, checks that a boundary function
exists for every resolved direction, and then builds the modules in a fixed order. Nothing is filled with data yet:
that is initialization (@sec-ch01-initialization).

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** N/A, a code map: resolve the grid, check the boundary list, build the modules in `reset`.

**Data.** In: a `MeshBlockOptions` tree. Out: the module objects and the two float64 stage buffers, unfilled.

**Placement.** Once, at block construction, before initialization.

**Activation.** Always; no construction switch.

**Guarantee / limits.** A map of control flow and ownership; no convergence order.

**Evidence.** `test_yaml_keys.<b>`: an unknown key is refused with its path (exact substring); not run here.
:::

### Derivation

No separate derivation: this section describes an interface or control-flow path, and the operators are derived
in their owning chapters.

### Numerical method

The constructor `MeshBlockImpl::MeshBlockImpl` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::MeshBlockImpl >}})
resolves the global grid first, because the output-slice checks read it before any coordinate object exists. It then
requires at least two, four or six boundary functions for one, two or three resolved directions, and calls `reset`.
`MeshBlockImpl::reset` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reset >}}) builds these, in order. The layout
and its exchange buffers (and checks that the layout's world size matches its partitioning, with the six-panel factor
on the cubed sphere). The internal block boundaries, where a face owned by a neighbour or by a periodic wrap loses its
boundary function (@sec-ch11-registry). The outputs, where every slice coordinate must lie in the global half-open bounds, a slice list must be strictly
increasing, and a slice cannot be combined with a sum on the same axis. There `pnetcdf` without `PNETCDF=ON` and an unsupported type are refused.
Then come the integrator and the coordinates. Then the hydro module, which must have at least one variable, and the
scalar module, whose reconstruction inherits the horizontal hydro one when the card omits it
(`MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml`, {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}). Last
come the internal (solid) boundary and the two step-start buffers `u0` and `s0`, float64 tensors of shape (variables,
$x_3$, $x_2$, $x_1$[^rg-e646ebd1a056]). Construction approximates no operator and has no convergence order.

@fig-ch01-construction-flow shows the call sequence.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch01-construction-flow
#| fig-cap: "Construct a MeshBlock and its modules. Labelled green boxes name operations or owners; black arrows show the reading sequence, not a timing measurement."
#| fig-alt: "Sequence: layout / boundaries; outputs; integrator / coordinates; hydro / scalar / solids; stage registers."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch01.figures.fig_construction_flow import make_fig
make_fig()
```

**Why the order of `reset` is what it is.** Each step of the sequence needs the one before it.

1. The global grid is resolved first, because the output-slice checks compare against the global bounds before any
   coordinate object exists ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::MeshBlockImpl >}}).
2. The layout comes before the boundaries, because a face is physical only if no neighbour owns it, and the layout is
   what says who the neighbours are ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reset >}}).
3. The integrator and coordinates come before the hydro module, which reads both when it builds its stencils. The
   scalar module comes after the hydro module, whose horizontal reconstruction it may inherit.
4. The stage buffers come last, sized by the hydro and scalar variable counts, which exist only now.

1. Resolve the global grid and check the boundary list: `MeshBlockImpl`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::MeshBlockImpl >}}).
2. Build the layout, boundaries, outputs and modules: `reset` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reset >}}).
3. Read the card into the options tree: `from_yaml`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).

**How to use it.** A minimal card names the grid and leaves every boundary at its default, `reflecting`:

To implement another equation-of-state type, follow @sec-ch02-new-eos.

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `geometry`[^rg-309d46a42a40], `type`[^rg-aa05c4fa92f5], `cells`[^rg-87eb36db6ba0], `nx1`[^rg-205782379230], `nx2`[^rg-bc5bbd81137a], `nx3`[^rg-ba7bec301dc2], `nghost`[^rg-61a40b696c3f], `boundary-condition`[^rg-b8d05d2e0b8b], `external`[^rg-3c596d26d7e7], `x1-inner`[^rg-a3aacff1589c], `x1-outer`[^rg-cb63f03cceb3], `dynamics`[^rg-bfe1dcdd7a8f], `equation-of-state`[^rg-d7418324442e].
```yaml
geometry:
  type: cartesian
  cells: {nx1: 64, nx2: 1, nx3: 1, nghost: 3}
boundary-condition:
  external: {x1-inner: reflecting, x1-outer: outflow}
dynamics:
  equation-of-state: {type: ideal-gas}  # the default, moist-mixture, needs a thermodynamics block
```

Refused at construction: a boundary name that is not registered (@sec-ch11-registry), and fewer boundary functions
than the resolved directions need. Also refused: a layout whose world size does not match its partitioning, and an
output slice outside the global bounds, a slice list that is not strictly increasing, or a slice combined with a sum
on the same axis. An unsupported output type and a hydro
model with no variable are refused too. In C++ the call is one line,
`MeshBlock block(MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml(card))`, which runs the constructor
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::MeshBlockImpl >}}) and `reset`; from Python,
`snapy.MeshBlock(snapy.MeshBlockOptions.from_yaml(card))` (@sec-ch01-python).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The layout's world size must match its partitioning, with the panel factor on the cubed sphere. Unsupported
output types, parallel NetCDF without `PNETCDF=ON`, and a hydro model with no variable are rejected in `reset`;
no setup execution is claimed here.
:::

[^rg-f2bec48375b7]: YAML — YAML Ain't Markup Language, the structured input format used for decks

[^rg-e646ebd1a056]: $x_1, x_2, x_3$ — the three coordinate directions; $x_1$ is always the vertical (radial) direction

[^rg-309d46a42a40]: geometry — coordinate-system and grid options

[^rg-aa05c4fa92f5]: type — implementation selector for the enclosing options block

[^rg-87eb36db6ba0]: cells — cell counts and ghost-width options

[^rg-205782379230]: nx1 — number of cells in the first coordinate direction

[^rg-bc5bbd81137a]: nx2 — number of cells in the second coordinate direction

[^rg-ba7bec301dc2]: nx3 — number of cells in the third coordinate direction

[^rg-61a40b696c3f]: nghost — number of ghost cells at each boundary

[^rg-b8d05d2e0b8b]: boundary-condition — boundary options: `external` boundary-function names for the domain faces and `internal` solid-cell settings

[^rg-3c596d26d7e7]: external — boundary-function names for external domain faces

[^rg-a3aacff1589c]: x1-inner — boundary name on the inner first-coordinate face

[^rg-cb63f03cceb3]: x1-outer — boundary name on the outer first-coordinate face

[^rg-bfe1dcdd7a8f]: dynamics — hydrodynamic options block

[^rg-d7418324442e]: equation-of-state — equation-of-state options
